newsitem.title: JAPAN: NCB says mulling specifics of capital increase.
newsitem.headline: NCB says mulling specifics of capital increase.

text.p: Nippon Credit Bank Ltd (NCB) said on Friday that it was still considering specific details of a planned increase in its capital and had absolutely no plan to reduce its capital.
The bank also said in a statement that it would make utmost efforts to resume dividend payments as soon as possible.
The Japanese business daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun said on Friday that new shares in NCB, to be issued as part of a rescue package for the troubled bank, would be priced below the market.

Banking sources said on Friday that the Ministry of Finance (MOF) had asked top commercial banks and long-term credit banks to purchase the new shares in NCB at a price of about 60 percent of the market value.

A MOF official told Reuters earlier this week that new shares would be priced based on a value of around 50 yen, which would be the value of the existing 1.8 billion shares after using 300 billion yen to write off non-performing loans.

Nippon Credit Bank on Tuesday announced restructuring measures aimed at restoring its financial health. It said it hoped the measures, which included halting overseas operations, would boost its capital by 300 billion yen.

Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka said on Tuesday that the ministry had asked the Bank of Japan and a special body administering a fund to wind up failed finance firms for permission to use the fund to buy preferred stock to be issued by NCB.
